advanced: Advanced mode lets you type any value, also outside the normal range, and shows extra settings. Each stage remembers its own on/off.
clickTool: Pick what a left-click does. Connect face (green): the connector attaches to this face; works on any tool object. Avoid face (red): nothing grows into the face, and the gap number pushes the zone outward. Avoid object (red): the whole object is kept clear, grown by the gap number. Right-click clears a green or red item. Shift-click is a shortcut for the avoid mode.
boltClearance: Keeps room above the screw heads so a screwdriver can reach them. Diameter is the screw head plus margin; Height is the head height plus margin. Slot runs the clearance outward from the flange centre so inner screws stay reachable; Cylinder keeps clear only straight above each head. The numbers show the real size in mm.
printable: Prints with the flange face on the bed and no supports: nothing grows below the bed, and every part rests on material below it (45° overhang at most). Test feature.
bridge: Bridge is instant: a solid wrap from the flange top to the green faces, narrower in the middle, minus the red zones, the robot side, Flange Clearance and Bolt Clearance. It updates by itself after every change. Waist: how much narrower the middle is than a straight wrap (0 = straight).
smoothing: Each Smooth click rounds the voxel steps a little more and keeps the volume. Connect surfaces stay in place. Smoothing fills the red zones a little, so finish with Re-cut clearances. Generate resets smoothing.
reCut: Cuts the clearance zones out of the final shape again, like a boolean difference. Connect surfaces are never cut. Use it after smoothing, or after changing a gap.
refinement: Always start with Draft: it designs the connector and clears the red zones, fast. Normal and Fine then refine that Draft on a finer voxel. Normal unlocks after Draft has finished, Fine after Normal (hover a greyed button to see what is needed). Finished levels are kept, so you can click between Draft, Normal and Fine to compare them. If you change the objects, faces, clearances or the load settings, you start again at Draft.
materialAmount: How much of the design space may be filled with material. More = stronger and heavier. The grams next to it are an estimate of the first-pass weight (design space volume × amount × PLA density); the real result is shown after Generate. Green = recommended range.
voxelTarget: Voxel size of the Fine level, in mm. Smaller = more detail but much slower. Normal is halfway between the Draft voxel (about 1.5 mm) and this value. Example: target 1.0 gives Normal 1.25 and Fine 1.0.
